extracted.intended_audience: academic researchers and prospective grant applicants in advertising/marketing; policymakers and institutional leaders interested in advertising research funding
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the stated purposes and evaluative aims of the American Association of Advertising Agencies (A.A.A.A.) Educational Foundation when funding research (goals articulated when chartered in 1967 and applied to 22 grants awarded 1968–1973). Useful for applicants, evaluators, and historians assessing alignment with the foundation's objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a bridge between advertising and university research
rubrics_metrics.description: To create a bridge between advertising and university research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation pursued this by funding a research program in areas of marketing, advertising, and consumer behavior; the digest documents 22 funded grants (1968–1973) that exemplify this bridge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attract top young people to the study of advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: To attract top young people to the study of advertising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied mechanisms include funding research projects and supporting academic pathways that make advertising an appealing and rigorous field of study for promising students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raise the academic stature of advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: To raise the academic stature of advertising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation measures progress toward this goal through funded research output, continued projects, and efforts such as establishing endowed chairs at graduate business schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlarge the body of knowledge about advertising and the consumer
rubrics_metrics.description: To enlarge the body of knowledge about advertising and the consumer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The digest highlights significant contributions to knowledge areas including the economics of advertising, consumer decision processes, market segmentation, and how advertising is perceived; success is evidenced by resulting books, monographs, articles, dissertations, and working papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document the advertising industry's positions with government
rubrics_metrics.description: To document the advertising industry's positions with government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research funded by the Foundation was expected to provide documented evidence and analyses that could articulate or support the industry's positions in policy or regulatory contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work toward establishing chairs of advertising at graduate business schools
rubrics_metrics.description: To work toward establishing chairs of advertising at graduate business schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-term institutional objective; establishment of academic chairs viewed as a structural means to raise the field's stature and sustain research and teaching capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible topical scope: marketing, advertising, and consumer behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Funded research should fall within the areas of marketing, advertising, and consumer behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation's research program was explicitly focused on these disciplinary areas; proposals addressing these topics would align with the Foundation's remit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected research outputs and dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Research was expected to produce publishable outputs: books, monographs, articles, dissertations, and working papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The digest supplies bibliographies of published material resulting from each grant, indicating an expectation that funded work lead to tangible scholarly and public-facing publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Success measured by achievement of stated goals through funded research
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation judges success by how well funded grants achieve the stated goals (first five goals noted as considerably advanced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report states the Foundation 'has achieved considerable success in achieving the first five goals by the funding of a research program' — implying an evaluative criterion that funded projects should demonstrably advance those goals.
